title: The Nitratidesulfovibrio sp. and Thermodesulfomicrobium sp.: Isolated Sulfate‐Reducing Bacteria From Ahvaz Oilfield in Khouzestan
content:
Applying a combinatorial workflow consisting of a culture-dependent, molecular approach, and meta-analysis, we isolated SRB taxa with low incidence in oilfields.


ABSTRACT

The petroleum importance to human beings highlights the oil reservoirs' microbiology significance. It is crucial to develop remediation strategies, especially for sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB). Accordingly, this work aimed to isolate, characterize, and enumerate SRB from industrial water samples in Ahvaz and compare the results with meta-analysis. Following the enrichment at Postgate's B medium (PGB) and viable cell counting by the MPN statistical approach, a PCR amplification was performed. Beside verifying the SRB contamination via FeS formation, a high bacterial load was confirmed by MPN. The rare incidence of isolates, that is, Nitratidesulfovibrio liaohensis and Thermodesulfomicrobium ‌‌sp., in oil-contaminated environs was confirmed by a meta-analysis report. Although the SRB rapid detection and precise quantification have been investigated extensively, this work could be considered a milestone for SRB distribution in Ahvaz, Khuzestan, as a significant oil reservoir. More studies could also complete the results to develop potent inhibitors regarding biocide resistance in region.
